column1: # Automatic live-conversion commit scenarios.
# Read by:
#   windows/crates/shared/src/conversion_policy.rs   (parity test around
#                                                     find_auto_commit_live_conversion_snapshot)
#   scripts/check-input-policy-parity.ps1
# This rule has exactly one implementation: `conversion_policy.rs`, reached on
# Android through the shared engine (`op=autoCommit`). Android keeps no second
# copy, so a scenario only has to describe the shared behaviour.
# Format: id<TAB>reading<TAB>preview<TAB>history<TAB>expect
#   reading  current hiragana composition (kana only)
#   preview  live-conversion baseline for the whole reading
#   history  `readingCount:surface` entries separated by `;`
#            readingCount = kana characters of that snapshot's reading,
#            surface = the preview shown at that point (a prefix of `preview`)
#   expect   `none` or `<readingLength>:<surfacePrefix>`
# A snapshot's reading is the current reading's prefix of `readingCount` kana and
# the last surface equals `preview`, so the data has the shape a real inference
# sequence produces.
# The romaji-split rule is exercised by unit tests instead of here; it depends on
# the raw romaji index, which these kana-only readings do not carry.
# ---- A stable clause prefix is committed --------------------------------------
# わたしはがっこうにいって = 12 kana, so 10 stay uncommitted. 私は学校に行って
# ends in the particle て and the next clause starts with 勉, a natural boundary
# that every later preview keeps as a prefix.
auto_commit_stable_clause
column2: わたしはがっこうにいってべんきょうしています
column3: 私は学校に行って勉強しています
column4: 4:私は;8:私は学校;9:私は学校に;12:私は学校に行って;14:私は学校に行って勉;17:私は学校に行って勉強;18:私は学校に行って勉強し;19:私は学校に行って勉強して;22:私は学校に行って勉強しています

column1: # A clause ending in Japanese punctuation is a natural boundary even when the next
# character is not a content word.
auto_commit_punctuation_clause
column2: きょうはいいてんきですね。あしたはあめです
column3: 今日はいい天気ですね。明日は雨です

auto_commit_short_reading

column1: # U+FA11 (﨑) is a compatibility ideograph and is in the shared class list. The only
# natural boundary here ends in て, and its prefix contains 﨑 as the only kanji.
# Later snapshots end in a kanji, so this one is the longest match.
auto_commit_compat_ideograph
